the use of milk as a serum substitute in the culture of fibroblasts and with the growth requirements for normal and transformed fibrobastic cells in this medium.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fibroblasts transformed to a more aggressive phenotype by a variety of mechanisms are capable of growing in serum-free medium, whereas nontransformed fibrolasts require serum for growth.
milk contains factors that are necessary for the growth of certain types of transformed cells, but that these factors are not sufficient for normal cell growth.
fibronectin is a critical factor in serum-free growth of fibroblasts.

fibronectin is required for the growth of transformed fibroblastic lines and cell lines in serum-free medium.
fibroblastic transformation is associated with a change in the cell's requirement for attachment factors.
milk is a useful supplement for the growth of certain transformed cells in serum-free medium.
